items.item_text: Job offer is contingent upon satisfactory clearance based on Background Check results.

The Campus Energy Performance Manager position serves as the campus lead for energy performance and is responsible for advancing UC San Diego's energy, climate, and resilience objectives through strategic planning, performance analysis, and cross-functional implementation leadership. The role develops and maintains the University's Strategic Energy Plan, leads energy-related components of the Sustainability & Climate Action Plan, and evaluates opportunities to improve energy performance, reduce utility costs, enhance resiliency, and support institutional climate commitments.

Using advanced analytical, planning, and project management skills, the position assesses campus utility and building performance; develops business cases and long-term energy strategies; and maintains a portfolio of operational, maintenance, capital, policy, and technology opportunities that support energy optimization and emissions reduction. The role provides guidance on emerging energy technologies, electrification, renewable energy, battery storage, demand flexibility, utility transformation, and regulatory developments.

Working across Facilities Management, Utilities & Sustainability, Capital Programs, Sustainability, and other campus partners, the position facilitates implementation of strategic energy initiatives, monitors progress toward institutional goals, and advises leadership on balancing operational reliability, financial stewardship, resilience, and sustainability objectives.

Advanced ability to assess needs for energy management products to meet those needs. Comprehensive knowledge of heating, steam, and heat transfer systems, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC), power, and electrical services. Demonstrated ability to evaluate energy performance, identify opportunities and prioritize actions based on various criteria such as financial impact, reliability, resiliency, risk, and climate goals.
Advanced knowledge of one or more of the following areas: natural gas, biomethane, carbon management, energy efficiency, direct access and / or wholesale electric power.

Comprehensive knowledge of energy efficient design, operations, and evaluations of institutional facilities and systems, and programs. Ability to monitor systems and implement corrective action on an ongoing basis. Comprehensive ability to work within building automation systems and controls systems; with ability to review trends, programs, and make recommendations for changes in programming, software, and hardware.
Advanced conceptual and planning skills. Proven ability in strategic energy and climate planning. Proven ability to critically analyze information, communications, and reports.

Advanced understanding of how programs relate to other business strategies and initiatives. Advanced ability to interpret policy and ensure alignment to related processes and procedures. Proven ability to establish and recommend changes to policies and operations based on thorough analysis and understanding of impact to other business areas in the University.

Advanced communication, organization, and project management skills. Advanced ability to facilitate change related to energy and climate, with strong verbal, written and technology based skills. Strong ability to adapt information for different audiences. Proven ability to convey technical information in a concise manner. Proven project management skills.

Advanced ability to work in a collaborative manner to achieve results. Demonstrated ability to create a positive environment with staff at all levels of the institution in the area of energy reduction, optimization, and efficiency. Demonstrated ability to create and articulate goals clearly that lead to measurable results.

Excellent interpersonal skills, including tact, diplomacy, and flexibility to work with faculty, executive administration, consultants, and general public. Proven ability to represent the University in systemwide workgroups and related meetings.
